correctness.rationale: The augmented simplicial Lefschetz identity assigns each setwise fixed face, union of q vertex orbits, signed contribution (-1)^(q-1), including the empty face as -1; thus reduced L(g)=-I(B_g,-1). For r^k, h=gcd(n,k), its conflict graph is C_h, K2 (h=2), or empty (h=1), so I(B,-1)=2cos(pi h/3). For r^k s, reflection orbits produce P_{(n-1)/2}, P_{n/2+1}, or P_{n/2-2}, including n=3 and the n=4 empty case. The path recurrence a0=1,a1=0,a_t=a_(t-1)-a_(t-2) gives the second character. Homology concentration and ranks are known from Donovan–Scoville Proposition 5.4. Irreducibility for 3|n and D_n-invariant dimensions follow by finite group character algebra. Reconstructed all cases analytically and checked direct signed face traces independently for every dihedral element n=3..16 (266), plus group invariant averages; 2014 Alexander-dual formulas independently reproduce all 10,098 characters n=3..100. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove infinitely many cases.
residual_risks: Finite verification is not an all-n proof; the supplied Lefschetz orbit argument and the old homology concentration yield the unbounded claim.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Let K=Ind(C_n) on the same n cyclic labels. Its minimal nonfaces are the n adjacent pairs {i,i+1}. The maximal faces of its combinatorial Alexander dual K^vee are therefore their n complements, all n−2-consecutive-vertex cyclic intervals; by 2014 Definition 3.2, K^vee=N(n,n−3) exactly and D_n-equivariantly, not merely up to homotopy. Björner–Tancer combinatorial Alexander duality identifies H~_d(K;Q) with H~^{n−d−3}(N(n,n−3);Q). The complement shuffle signs make this identification equivariant after tensoring by the sign of the permutation of all n vertices. For n=3m, N(n,n−3) is in Proposition 7.2 with l=m−1 and carries the signed 3-point augmentation representation (rank 2); for n=3m+1 or 3m+2 it is in Proposition 7.3 with l=m−1 and carries a line with r=1 and s=(-1)^m. The sign twist yields EXACTLY the assigned rotation/reflection characters in all congruence cases, and hence the irreducibility and n≡1,11 mod 12 invariant criterion. No new equivariant equivalence is postulated; this is a direct dual identification and old full representation theorem. A separate independently produced all-n signed fixed-orbit proof does not make the covered claim original.
